# dsm_user_home_service (Resource)

Manages the DSM user home service, which creates per-user home folders under the `homes` shared folder. This is a single NAS-wide setting, so only one instance of this resource should exist per DSM host.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dsm_user_home_service" "homes" {
  location           = "/volume1"
  enable_recycle_bin = true

  # Keep this NAS-wide service enabled if the Terraform resource is removed.
  disable_on_destroy = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `location` (String) Volume path hosting the `homes` shared folder, e.g. `/volume1`. Must be a path: a bare volume name such as `volume1` is rejected by DSM with error 3101.

### Optional

- `disable_on_destroy` (Boolean) Whether `terraform destroy` should actually turn the service off. Defaults to `false`, in which case destroy only drops the resource from state and leaves DSM untouched. Disabling the service is a NAS-wide action: it takes personal folders away from every user and breaks Synology Drive and Photos, which depend on them. Files under the `homes` shared folder are not deleted either way.
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether the user home service is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
- `enable_recycle_bin` (Boolean) Enable the recycle bin on the `homes` shared folder. Defaults to `false`.
- `force` (Boolean) Pass the `force` flag to DSM to proceed past soft warnings (for example when Synology Drive or Photos already depend on the home service). Defaults to `false`. Not read back from DSM.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Fixed identifier of this singleton resource (`user_home_service`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import dsm_user_home_service.homes user_home_service
```
